question_text:
A zinc single crystal is being pulled in tension, with the normal to its basal plane (0001) at $60^{\circ}$ to the tensile axis and with the slip direction [1120] at $40^{\circ}$ to the tensile axis.
(a) What is the resolved shear stress, $\tau$, acting in the slip direction when a tensile stress of $0.690 \mathrm{MPa}(100 \mathrm{psi})$ is applied?
(b) What tensile stress is necessary to reach the critical resolved shear stress, $\tau_{c}$, of $0.94 \mathrm{MPa}(136 \mathrm{psi})$?

Give your answers as a tuple: (resolved shear stress, tensile stress)The units of each required answer are (MPa,MPa), respectively.
response:
Using Schmid's law: $\tau = \sigma \cos\phi \cos\lambda$, where $\phi = 60°$ (angle between slip-plane normal and tensile axis) and $\lambda = 40°$ (angle between slip direction and tensile axis).

**(a)** $\tau = 0.690 \cos 60° \cos 40° = 0.690 \times 0.5 \times 0.7660 = 0.264 \text{ MPa}$

**(b)** $\sigma = \dfrac{\tau_c}{\cos\phi \cos\lambda} = \dfrac{0.94}{0.5 \times 0.7660} = 2.45 \text{ MPa}$

$$\boxed{(0.264,\ 2.45)}$$
